40_marg2216: Uzziah, also called Azariah, reigned in Jerusalem over the two tribes fifty-two years. 40_marg2268: In memory of Belus was consecrated the idol called Bel, and by this name the prophets often call the idol of Babylon. The Sidonians often call him Baal or Baalim. Baal means “having,” Baalim “having me.” Hence women too call their husbands Baalim, that is, my husband, namely the one who has me in marriage. But in the Hebrew tongue a husband is called is, and a wife issa. So it is said here that the believing people, wishing to show me to be her husband, will call me is, that is, husband, not Baalim, which likewise means my husband: for though by its etymology it could be said, yet out of hatred of idols it ought not to be said, lest in the worship of God we recall the name of idols, and lest, while she names her husband, she think of the idol, as could happen through the ambiguity of the word.
